text.p: Following are the main stories in today's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said Malaysia's drive to develop did not mean that it was spending beyond its means. The country had to develop more rapidly as it had lagged behind during the colonial period.
-- Private television channel TV3 will start 24-hour transmission on Sept 1.
-- The issue of regional currency speculation may be raised at the Commonwealth Finance Ministers meeting in Mauritius next month, said Commonwealth secretary-general Chief Emeka Anyaoku.
-- PM Mahathir said Malaysians may lose their country one day if they continue to depend heavily on foreign workers.

-- Locally-incorporated foreign banks which offer custodial share services to foreign clients have asked for immediate payment from brokers upon delivery of share-scrip following the implementation of a shorter settlement period from Monday.
